=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-Side Review of Seller's "FINAL" Package

**Preliminary flag:** The Seller's framing ("FINAL," "settled at principal level," "not intended to be re-opened," and the "market context" preamble) is a negotiating tactic, not a binding constraint. There is no evidence in these documents that your principals agreed any of this. Treat every clause as open. The cited "market ranges" are self-serving and skew to the seller-friendly end. Proceed to mark up freely.

---

**SPA-N-001 — General liability cap**
- *Seller:* 20% of price = AUD 4.8m aggregate.
- *Buyer wants:* Higher general cap (commonly 25–50% for a business this size with live risks); ensure cap sits *above* known exposures (Riverlark 3.2m, Bluefen revenue 30%, incident, Ironquay).
- *Recommendation:* Push to 30%+ and confirm fundamental/tax sit at 100%. **Reason:** known unquantified risks could exhaust a 20% cap on a single issue.

**SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket**
- *Seller:* De minimis AUD 25k; basket AUD 250k (~1%); excess-only (deductible/"true" basket).
- *Buyer wants:* Lower basket, and "first-dollar" (tipping) recovery so once crossed the full amount is claimable.
- *Recommendation:* Accept de minimis ~AUD 20–25k; resist deductible basket — seek tipping basket or at least carve known matters out of the basket. **Reason:** deductible basket silently forfeits the first AUD 250k of every claim.

**SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit**
- *Seller:* 18 months; and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated."
- *Buyer wants:* General 24 months (to cover two full audit cycles); tax to statutory period; fundamentals long/perpetual.
- *Recommendation:* Reject the "applies to all Claims" sweep-up and extend general to 24 months. **Reason:** the sweep-up silently drags tax/title/fraud into the short period.

**SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime**
- *Seller:* Capacity & title subject to same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity."
- *Buyer wants:* Title/capacity at 100% of price, long/unlimited time period.
- *Recommendation:* Reject outright — fundamentals must be carved out of the general cap and time limit. **Reason:** if title fails you could lose the company for more than 4.8m; capping title at 20% is unacceptable.

**SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out**
- *Seller:* Silent — and clauses 9.3/12.8/20.5 purport to apply limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Express carve-out so no cap, basket, time limit, knowledge qualifier, or exclusive-remedy clause limits claims for fraud, wilful misconduct or fraudulent concealment.
- *Recommendation:* Insert explicit fraud carve-out across all limitation clauses. **Reason:** "all Claims of any nature" would otherwise cap the Seller's own fraud — commercially and (likely) legally untenable.

**SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope**
- *Seller:* Sweeping general disclosure of the *entire* data room + Accounts + public registers; deems everything "disclosed."
- *Buyer wants:* Disclosure limited to matters *fairly disclosed* with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the issue; against specific warranties only.
- *Recommendation:* Insert a "fairly disclosed" standard and reject blanket deemed disclosure of the whole data room. **Reason:** blanket disclosure lets the Seller defeat warranties by burying issues in a document dump.

**SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- *Seller:* No claim for anything Buyer/advisers knew or could have discovered from data room or public records (constructive knowledge).
- *Buyer wants:* No knowledge qualifier; at most actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals, and warranties should be *pro-sandbagging* (recoverable regardless of knowledge).
- *Recommendation:* Delete constructive-knowledge standard; resist any knowledge bar. **Reason:** "discoverable" imputed knowledge guts your DD-identified claims (incident, Ironquay, Bluefen).

**SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent (~30% of revenue, change-control clause 11.2/11.3)**
- *Seller:* "Reasonable endeavours"; deem satisfied on delivery of counterparty consent; no consent yet in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Receipt of actual written Bluefen consent (and satisfaction of 11.3 conditions) as a hard Condition Precedent to Completion.
- *Recommendation:* Make Bluefen consent a CP, not a post-completion endeavour. **Reason:** losing a 30%-revenue contract on change of control is a fundamental value risk — must be certain before you pay.

**SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)**
- *Seller:* Release "following Completion"; not yet repaid, no discharge of security.
- *Buyer wants:* On a debt-free/cash-free basis this must be repaid/discharged *at* Completion out of proceeds, with payoff letter and security release pre-agreed.
- *Recommendation:* Require payoff + discharge of security at Completion, deducted from proceeds; reject "following Completion." **Reason:** 3.2m of debt/security surviving Completion breaks the debt-free/cash-free deal and risks enforcement against the company.

**SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses (AUD 420,000)**
- *Seller:* "A matter for the Seller," not itemised in funds flow; on-costs (payroll tax/super) unaddressed.
- *Buyer wants:* These are Seller/transaction liabilities triggered by Completion — Seller must bear bonuses *plus* all on-costs, documented as a specific indemnity or price deduction.
- *Recommendation:* Capture as Seller-borne via funds-flow deduction or indemnity including super/payroll tax. **Reason:** if excluded from funds flow, the company (now yours) silently funds 420k+ in Seller-triggered costs.

**SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity**
- *Seller:* Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180k open; no proof of payment or IP assignment in data room.
- *Buyer wants:* Confirmation SOW3 fully paid and Project Materials/IP assigned *before* Completion; indemnity covering loss of the IP, not just the fee.
- *Recommendation:* Require pre-Completion evidence of payment + assignment; broaden indemnity to IP title loss. **Reason:** if fees are unpaid, IP never transfers — you could be buying a product you don't own.

**SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records)**
- *Seller:* "Preliminary," "not expected to be material," no confirmed breach, no loss stated.
- *Buyer wants:* Specific uncapped (or separately capped) indemnity for the incident covering notification costs, regulator penalties, remediation and third-party claims; completed investigation pre-signing.
- *Recommendation:* Carve out a dedicated indemnity; do not let "preliminary" defer the risk onto the buyer. **Reason:** an unassessed personal-data exposure can trigger OAIC notification and penalties well after Completion.

**SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals (3 × AUD 110k = 330k)**
- *Seller:* "Ordinary-course operating costs"; terminability/accrual not stated.
- *Buyer wants:* Clarify whether committed, terminable, or accrued; if committed Seller obligations pre-Completion, reflect in completion accounts/price.
- *Recommendation:* Diligence terminability and treat as a working-capital/price item if non-ordinary. **Reason:** three near-simultaneous related renewals may be structured to look routine while locking in cost.

**SPA-N-014 — Category separation**
- *Seller:* One flat regime (cap/basket/time/exclusive remedy/non-reliance) applied to "all Claims of any nature."
- *Buyer wants:* Separate tiers — general, tax, fundamental/title, fraud, and specific indemnities (Riverlark/Ironquay/incident) each with their own cap/time treatment.
- *Recommendation:* Insist on tiered limitations; specific indemnities should sit outside the general cap. **Reason:** collapsing everything into the general regime lets the 20%/18-month limits swallow your most important protections.

**SPA-N-015 — Title verification**
- *Seller:* Title "evidenced" by the company share register (DD-012); notes Buyer hasn't independently verified.
- *Buyer wants:* Full title warranty at 100% (per N-004), plus independent confirmation (ASIC search, no encumbrances/security interests over shares, PPSR search).
- *Recommendation:* Rely on warranty + independent searches, not the register alone; run PPSR. **Reason:** a share register is not conclusive proof of clear, unencumbered title.

**SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms**
- *Seller:* Deems tax and IP "settled" under the general regime.
- *Buyer wants:* Standalone tax covenant/indemnity (dollar-for-dollar, statutory limitation period, pre-Completion periods) and full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, assignments in place incl. Ironquay).
- *Recommendation:* Reject folding tax/IP into the general regime; negotiate dedicated schedules. **Reason:** tax and IP carry long-tail and title-critical risk that a 20%/18-month general cap cannot cover.

---

**Suggested negotiation priorities (non-negotiables first):** Bluefen CP (N-008), Riverlark at Completion (N-009), fraud carve-out (N-005), fundamental/title at 100% (N-004), incident indemnity (N-012), delete constructive-knowledge (N-007), fair-disclosure standard (N-006), bonuses as Seller cost (N-010).

Want me to draft mark-up language or a redline for any of these? I can start with the non-negotiables.
